spec.name: Baba Yaga's Hut on Chicken Legs
spec.description: A Slavic folk-art diorama of Baba Yaga's hut: a carved log cabin standing on two scaly golden chicken legs, with a steep teal-shingled roof, a rooster-head ridge finial, glowing carved windows and a wooden staircase descending from the door.
spec.layout: The hut faces +Z. At the bottom, two golden chicken legs rise from the ground (their big three-toed feet with cream claws rest on y=0, toes spread, moss tufts and two amber mushrooms at the footpads) and vanish under the hut floor at y=1.4. The log cabin sits between y=1.4 and y=2.75: a plank floor platform, then seven courses of round logs 2.0 m wide (x) by 2.2 m deep (z), cut log ends showing bright at the four corners. The front wall (z=+1.08) carries a tall plank door with iron ring and architrave, two carved windows with red-orange nalichniki, cream frames, shutters and warm glowing panes, and a carved staircase with posts descending from the door threshold to the ground at the front. Above the walls, a steep gabled roof runs front-to-back with overlapped teal shingles, a heavy ridge pole ending in a carved rooster-head finial facing +Z, two folk-patterned gable boards at the front and back, and a small plank chimney with pale smoke puffs, to y=3.9. Slavic folk style shows everywhere as chip-carved zigzags, rosettes and sun symbols in red, gold and green painted trim over weathered wood; every carved motif is a small part in its own colour seated on the wood surfaces.

parts.builds: Two golden chicken legs carrying the hut, one per side. Each: a thick scaly shank from mount hutFloor (y=1.45, where it disappears under the cabin floor) down to a knobbly knee at y=0.8, a slimmer scaly shank down to a bulging ankle at y=0.3, then the foot. Build the shanks as chained tubes along the leg joints (legL/kneeL/ankleL, legR/kneeR/ankleR) with overlapping scale bands: main colour 'scale', a ring of darker 'scaleDark' scales at the knee bulge and the ankle bulge, an 'ink' seam ring at each joint. Each knee gets a small back-pointing spur cone. The foot (rides footL/footR): a chunky 'foot' pad at y=0..0.12 with three forward toes spread from -0.35 to +0.35 rad around +Z, each toe a tapering tube with 'scale' top and 'foot' underside ending in a blunt 'cream' claw, plus a small rear dewclaw. At the footpads: 4-5 moss 'moss' tufts (small rounded blobs sunk into the ground) and two amber mushrooms (folk-red caps with cream spots, plank stems) tucked beside the toes.
parts.attaches: Top of each shank buried at mount hutFloor, under the cabin floor platform; all leg geometry rides joints legL/kneeL/ankleL/footL and legR/kneeR/ankleR/footR.

parts.builds: The log cabin body. A plank floor platform from y=1.4 to y=1.56, 2.1 x 2.3 m (x by z) of 'plank' boards with 'ink' seams between boards, its edge showing 'logEnd'. Above it, seven courses of round logs (diameter 0.17, axes alternating x and z) from y=1.56 to y=2.75 spanning x ±1.0 and z ±1.0 in 'log', each log's cut end a 'logEnd' disc showing at the four corners with 'ink' ring lines for growth rings; the top course is the top plate that meets mount eaves. On the two side walls (x=±1.08) and the back wall (z=-1.08), one small square window each: cream frame, folk-green shutters, a warm 'glow' pane with thin lattice bars, a folk-gold rosette carved above it, all seated slightly proud of the log surface. A folk-red carved trim board with chip-carved zigzag runs along the wall top just under mount eaves on all four sides.
parts.attaches: Sits on mount hutFloor (the chicken legs run up into its underside); its top plate is mount eaves where the roof sits; the front wall surface at z=+1.08 receives the door, front windows and stairs.

parts.builds: The hut's decorated front face and entry. A tall plank door (0.62 wide, from y=1.56 to y=2.15) of 'plank' boards with 'ink' plank seams, two 'folkGold' iron hinges and an iron ring handle, set in a carved architrave of 'folk' red with cream-painted chip-carved rosettes at the corners. Flanking the door, two windows at y=1.85..2.25, x=±0.62: 'cream' frames, red-orange 'folk' nalichniki boards with carved zigzag crowns above them, small green shutters swung open at ±25 deg, 'glow' panes with lattice bars, all seated on the front wall at z≈1.1 and protruding to z=1.18. A hanging lantern ('folk' frame, 'glow' light, folkGold cap) hangs by a short rod from the architrave beside the door at z=1.2. From mount threshold, a carved staircase: two 'plank' side stringers with folk-red carved edges, five treads with 'ink' seams descending from y=1.56 at z=1.12 to y=0.62 at z=1.8, supported by two thin posts reaching y=0, each post base ringed with 'moss'. A small 'plank' landing platform at the door threshold.
parts.attaches: Door and windows seat on the cabin front wall at z=+1.08; the staircase top meets mount threshold [0,1.56,1.08]; the lantern hangs from the door architrave; the two stair posts rest on the ground (floor true).

parts.builds: The steep gabled roof and its finials. Two slopes of overlapped shingles running front-to-back: from the eaves edge (x=±1.45, y=2.7) up to the ridge (x=0, y=3.8), shingles in 'shingle' laid in horizontal rows with 'shingleDark' shadow rows between them and a 'folkGreen' trim board along the eaves edge; the underside of each overhang shows 'plank' rafters. A heavy 'log' ridge pole along z from -1.5 to +1.5 at y=3.82 with 'logEnd' ends. At the front ridge end (z=+1.5) a carved rooster-head finial in 'plank' with folk-red comb, cream beak and eye, and a small wattle, facing +Z; a simple carved horse-head finial in 'plank' with a cream mane crest at the back ridge end facing -Z. Gable boards at the front and back (the triangular wall faces z=±1.12..1.45 under the slopes): 'cream' boards edged in 'folk' red with a large carved sun symbol ('folkGold') centred in each gable and chip-carved zigzag along the slopes. A small plank chimney ('plank', ink seams) rising through the back slope to y=3.7, capped with a folk-green band, with three pale 'smoke' puffs drifting up from it between y=3.7 and 3.85.
parts.attaches: Its base sits on the cabin's top plate at mount eaves; the slopes overhang the cabin walls on all sides; gable boards butt against the cabin's front and back walls; the chimney passes over the back slope.
